title: Activated charcoal and tea tree cold-process soap
subtitle: A deep-cleaning black bar for oily skin
excerpt: A cold-process bar with activated charcoal for a deep-cleansing action and tea tree essential oil for a clean, herbal scent. The charcoal gives the bar a dark grey-black colour and draws surface oils and impurities. Makes 7 bars.
sourceNotes: Activated charcoal in cold-process soap: general soapmaking reference. Tea tree essential oil antimicrobial properties: Carson, C. F. et al., Clinical Microbiology Reviews (2006, open access). Note: the adsorption action of activated charcoal is reduced by saponification; the cleansing effect in the finished bar is primarily physical (fine particle abrasion) rather than chemical adsorption. SAP values from SoapCalc.

recipe.batchNotes: Run any scale change through a lye calculator.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Two years in a cool dark cupboard once cured. The activated charcoal is chemically inert in the bar and does not affect shelf life. Discard if DOS or rancid smell appear.

glossaryTerms.definition: The reaction between fat and sodium hydroxide that produces soap and glycerine. Each oil has a SAP value: grams of lye per gram of oil.
The point at which soap batter thickens to thin-custard consistency. The signal to pour.
Charcoal processed at high temperature to create an extremely porous surface. In soap, it acts as a fine abrasive particle and gives the bar its distinctive dark grey or black colour.

projectSchedule.title: Unmould and cut
projectSchedule.body: Turn out the loaf. The bar will be a dark grey or black from the activated charcoal. The charcoal does not stain the hands; it rinses cleanly in use.

projectSchedule.title: Turn the bars
projectSchedule.body: Flip each bar on the rack. The charcoal colour is stable and does not fade.

projectSchedule.title: Four-week test
projectSchedule.body: Test a sliver. No sting means safe to use. The tea tree scent should be present but moderate.

projectSchedule.title: Cure complete
projectSchedule.body: A fully cured charcoal bar is firm and deeply dark. Store on an open rack.

content.text: A dark grey, deep-cleansing cold-process bar.
Activated charcoal
adds a very fine abrasive texture and the characteristic colour. Tea tree essential oil adds a clean, herbal scent. The
saponification
of the oil blend follows the same process as any standard CP bar; the charcoal and tea tree make this one most suited to oily or combination skin.
The charcoal will dust lightly when handling dry powder. Put on protective gloves and goggles before handling lye.
Ingredients

items.prepNote: calculated at 5% superfat for this oil blend
3% of oil weight; dispersed in a tablespoon of oil before adding
3% of oil weight; add at trace

content.text: Method
Mix lye solution
In a ventilated space with protective gloves and goggles on, add the sodium hydroxide to the distilled water. Stir until dissolved. Cool to 38 to 42°C.
Prepare oils and disperse charcoal

Melt coconut oil and shea butter. Add olive oil and castor oil. Cool to 38 to 42°C. Disperse the activated charcoal in two tablespoons of the oil blend to form a paste. This prevents charcoal speckling in the finished bar.
Blend to trace and add charcoal and essential oil
Pour the lye solution into the oils. Blend to light
trace
. Stir in the charcoal paste and tea tree essential oil by hand. The batter will turn dark grey immediately.
Pour and cure
Pour into the silicone mould. Wrap in a towel. Leave 48 hours. Unmould wearing protective gloves. Cut into bars. Cure 4 to 6 weeks.
Storage and shelf life
Two years in a cool dark cupboard on an open rack. The charcoal colour and the tea tree scent are both stable over the shelf life.
